correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the candidate distortion to the exact quotient \(f(t)=(5+2t+t^2)/(5+t^2)\) for \(t\ge0\). Its derivative has numerator \(2(5-t^2)\), giving exact minimum \(1\) at the axes and exact maximum \(1+1/\sqrt5\) at \(t=\sqrt5\). Zuo's Lemma 2.5 implies \(C_P(X)\le d_{\mathrm{BM}}(X,\ell_2^2)^2\), and Example 2.10 gives \(C_P(X)=1+1/\sqrt5\), so the matching upper bound is globally optimal.

value.rationale: The finding gives the exact Euclidean Banach–Mazur invariant of a classical finite-dimensional Cesàro section and proves that the Ptolemy lower bound is sharp there. It also certifies the globally optimal ellipse, ruling out all non-obvious linear coordinate changes. This is a natural geometric invariant of a standard Banach-sequence-space model rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
